Here is a response from ChatGPT 5.5 on the same question, and I appreciate that it showed me a direct derivation and answer that such a system (which is similar to what you showed me) is probably non-Lobian. I was wondering if you agree with it or could show me a similar set of derivations on your atlases setup.
Reconciled divergent operator analyses through Gödel-Tarski framework

Yes — the derivation is correct, and I can verify it line by line inside the atlas frames, because ChatGPT's setup and mine turn out to be the same frames: its "admissible refinement that doesn't arbitrarily discard established empirical constraints" is exactly the record-heredity condition from round one, so everything transfers without translation. But before running the derivations, one fork needs exposing, because it's the actual content of the comparison: ChatGPT's □* is not the operator I nominated as provability's analogue — it is Stab, the operator round four explicitly cast as truth's analogue. Recall the assignment: Stab plays True (external, unverifiable from inside, empty interior), 𝕃 plays Prov (internal, checkable, non-factive, provenance-carrying). Löb's theorem is a theorem about the second kind of thing — its classical proof runs through derivability conditions and a diagonal, properties of an internalized predicate. So the two answers don't collide; they fill different cells of a matrix that needs both. And the fact that the cells come out different — Löbian here, anti-Löbian there — is the system honoring the Gödel–Tarski split under transposition, not a disagreement about the system. Now the derivations.
Can you improve on GPT 5.5's work here to show me how one could actually encode models and domains as vectors?

Coda. The one-line improvement: GPT stipulated the vectors; the record bank derives them. And in physics the derivation is overdetermined — unit symmetry forces the domain axes (log ππ-groups), perturbation orders force the model rows (integer exponent vectors), tolerance forces the bias (log⁡εlogε) — so the bilinear ReLU gate is not a modeling choice but the leading-order normal form of empirical adequacy. The hand-drawn toy looked right because it was tracing a theorem.

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

class PaperMarkdownCompatibilityTests(unittest.TestCase):

        paper = (root / "paper.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertNotIn(
            r"\operatorname",
